title: Yuan dynasty
summary: The Mongols founded the Yuan dynasty, which ruled China from 1271 to 1368. Its first emperor, Kublai Khan, defeated the Southern Song in 1279, uniting China for the first time since the 9th century, and ruled from Dadu (modern Beijing). The Yuan favoured merchants and paper money, extended canals and roads, and sent armies against Japan and other neighbours to restore the tribute system. Corrupt, overtaxing government, floods and famines fed peasant risings until the Red Turban movement brought in the Ming in 1368.

uncertainty.note: Proclaimed in 1271 by Kublai Khan; Southern Song defeated in 1279 (AFE uses 1279 for complete reign); overthrown in 1368 by the Ming.

as_recorded.value: The Yuan Dynasty was established by the Mongols and ruled China from 1271 to 1368

related.because: The Mongol conquests begun by Genghis Khan enabled Kublai Khan to conquer the Song dynasty and proclaim the Yuan dynasty.
